story: The North Cascades are a jumble of steep, ice-carved peaks, built of rock that formed far away and was carried here on moving plates, then lifted and sculpted by glaciers. The park still holds more than three hundred of them, the most extensive glacier system in the lower forty-eight states, with nearly nine thousand feet of relief between its lowest valleys and Goode Mountain.

Moisture rules the park. Pacific storms drop enormous snowfalls on its western slopes and feed rainforest of cedar and hemlock in the valleys; across the crest the land turns drier, with pine and fire-adapted forest. The range of conditions gives the park more kinds of plants than any other national park.

Native peoples, among them the Upper Skagit and Chelan, travelled the passes for thousands of years. Miners and homesteaders came later; at Stehekin, reached only by boat or trail, an orchard planted by early settlers still bears fruit. In the twentieth century Seattle City Light dammed the Skagit, creating Diablo and Ross lakes, whose glacial flour colours them turquoise.
Congress created the park in 1968, together with the Ross Lake and Lake Chelan national recreation areas around it. The North Cascades Highway, completed in 1972, is the only road across it.

sightNotes.poi-north-cascades-diablo-lake-overlook: The best-known view in the park: a turquoise lake between forested peaks, beside the highway.
sightNotes.poi-north-cascades-cascade-pass: A climb to a high pass among glaciers and meadows, used by travellers for millennia.
sightNotes.poi-north-cascades-ross-lake: A long reservoir reached by trail from the highway, with a floating resort.
sightNotes.poi-north-cascades-gorge-creek-falls: A waterfall pouring into the Skagit gorge, seen from a short walk at the highway.
sightNotes.poi-north-cascades-thunder-knob: A short climb to views over Diablo Lake and the surrounding peaks.
sightNotes.poi-north-cascades-sourdough-mountain: A steep trail to a fire lookout high above Diablo.
sightNotes.poi-north-cascades-stehekin: A remote valley community at the head of Lake Chelan, reached by boat, plane or trail.
sightNotes.poi-north-cascades-rainbow-falls: A tall waterfall a short ride up the valley from Stehekin.
sightNotes.poi-north-cascades-buckner-orchard: A homestead orchard in the Stehekin valley, still producing apples.

entrances: The North Cascades Highway, WA 20, from Interstate 5 at Burlington in the west or from Winthrop in the east
Stehekin, by passenger ferry or floatplane up Lake Chelan; no road reaches it
Hozomeen, at the north end of Ross Lake, by road from Canada
permits: Overnight wilderness trips — a wilderness permit
lodging: North Cascades Lodge at Stehekin, and floating cabins at Ross Lake Resort
seasonalClosures: The highway's mountain section closes with snow, usually from November to April
camping: Harlequin Campground, reservable, with some first-come sites
Hozomeen Campground, first come, first served
Lakeview Campground, first come, first served
Lower Goodell Group Campground, reservable, with some first-come sites
Purple Point Campground, first come, first served

chronology.text: North Cascades National Park and its two national recreation areas are established.
The North Cascades Highway is completed.

safety: Glaciers and snowfields hide crevasses and avalanche danger; do not travel on them without training and equipment.
Store food properly: black bears live here.
regulations: Drones may not be launched, landed or flown in the park.

operatingHours: North Cascades National Park Service Complex is open year-round. The park operational season is late May-late September, with limited services outside the operational season. The North Cascades Visitor Center in Newhalem is open during the operational season, dates may vary annually.
weather: The best weather for visiting the North Cascades generally occurs between mid-June and late-September. Summer daytime temperatures average in the 70's F. Snow is off most trails by mid-July. Autumn and Spring are popular for color and wildlife. Storms are common: always be prepared for a few days of rain and wind. The east side of the Cascade Mountains (Lake Chelan National Recreation Area) is drier and warmer in the summer than the west side. Summer temperatures at Stehekin reach the 90's F.
directions: Access to North Cascades National Park and Ross Lake National Recreation Area is from the State Route 20 corridor. SR 20 (North Cascades Highway) connects with Interstate 5 (Exit 230) at Burlington. From the east, the highway intersects with US 97 at Okanogan and with SR 153 at Twisp. The State Department of Transportation closes a portion of the road between Ross Dam Trailhead and Lone Fir Campground in winter. The Lake Chelan National Recreation Area (Stehekin) is accessible by ferry or plane from Chelan.
